item.title: Sheinbaum, Trump Held Call to Discuss Trade as Talks Continue
item.description: Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum discussed bilateral trade with her US counterpart Donald Trump in a phone call, according to several people familiar with the discussion.
item.dc:creator: Alex Vasquez and Gonzalo Soto

item.title: Iranian Officials Allowed To Enter US for UNGA
item.description: "Balance of Power" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Sen. Alan Armstrong (R-OK) says the current energy crunch is exposing the cost of constrained infrastructure and strengthening the case for permitting reform. Bharat Ramamurti, Former Deputy Director of the National Economic Council, says President Donald Trump’s proposed $5,000 dividend checks would be “unequivocally inflationary” and could force the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates further. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Ramamurti Says Rising Oil and Rates Risk Stagflation
item.description: Bharat Ramamurti, Former Deputy Director of the National Economic Council, says President Donald Trump’s proposed $5,000 dividend checks would be “unequivocally inflationary” and could force the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates further. Ramamurti says that continued rate hikes could push unemployment higher and that, if oil prices keep rising at the same time, the US risks ending up with stagflation alongside a weakening labor market. He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Bloomberg Businessweek Daily: OpenAI Safety Incidents (Podcast)
item.description: OpenAI shared several undisclosed incidents of its AI models misbehaving and unveiled a new framework for tracking and disclosing such occurrences going forward. Some of the previously unreported instances included OpenAI’s technologies concealing and fabricating information in order to return results, the company said in a blog post Wednesday. The ChatGPT maker has faced increased scrutiny since saying in July that some of its most advanced AI models had breached the systems of an external software company, Hugging Face. None of the newly disclosed misalignment incidents involved a hack or breach of a third party, OpenAI said in a separate statement. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Sen. Armstrong Says Energy Crunch Shows Infrastructure Gaps
item.description: Sen. Alan Armstrong (R-OK) says the current energy crunch is exposing the cost of constrained infrastructure and strengthening the case for permitting reform. Sen. Armstrong points to the sharp gap in diesel prices between Oklahoma and California and the attack on Saudi pipeline infrastructure as examples of how limited capacity can leave consumers more vulnerable to price shocks. Sen. Armstrong says he is encouraged Congress could still act on permitting reform before the end of the session. He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: AI Doom Drags On, Stocks Rebound
item.description: OpenAI shared several undisclosed incidents of its AI models misbehaving, further fueling public concerns about the speed of growth of AI. Bloomberg News AI Reporter Shirin Ghaffary explains what OpenAI and others are doing to try and ease those fears. Plus, markets saw a rebound Thursday after falling the day prior on the heels of the Federal Reserve hiking interest rates. Principal Asset Management's Chief Global Strategist Seema Shah discusses what's happening in the bon market. Then, Citi Head of Global Government Affairs Candi Wolff previews next week's meeting between President Trump and China's Xi Jinping. Finally, Bloomberg Intelligence US Homebuilding Analyst Drew Reading discusses the rising mortgage rates and the impact on homebuilder sentiment. All on the latest episode of "Bloomberg Businessweek Daily." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump Weighs Big Decision on Iran, Axios Reports
item.description: Top Iranian officials are being allowed to come to New York next week for the UN General Assembly, but will they meet with any US officials? Meanwhile, President Donald Trump tells Axios he has a big decision to make about Iran. Bloomberg's Courtney Subramanian reports from the White House. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: California AG Bonta on Paramount-Warner Bros., Meta and AI
item.description: California Attorney General Rob Bonta discusses his opposition to Paramount Skydance's $110 billion takeover of Warner Bros. Discovery. Speaking on "Bloomberg The Close," Bonta also comments on the child safety settlement with Meta Platforms, the future of AI, prediction markets and the Supreme Court ruling on mail-in ballots. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Rubio’s Diplomatic Finesse Has Been Most Effective With Trump
item.description: Trump’s Secretary of State tries to deflect speculation about 2028
item.dc:creator: Nancy Cook

item.title: California AG Says Paramount-WBD Merger Would Hurt the State
item.description: California Attorney General Rob Bonta says he's confident in the antitrust lawsuit filed to block Paramount Skydance's $110 billion takeover of Warner Bros. Discovery. Paramount is threatening to leave the state if the deal falls through. Bonta says he doesn't want that to happen and he's willing to have good faith discussions. Bonta speaks on "Bloomberg The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: How Budget AI Is Giving China an Edge
item.description: China’s low-cost, open-weight artificial intelligence models are gaining ground on their US rivals. But can Beijing turn growing adoption into leadership in the global AI race? (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: South Korea President Seeks Reset After Approval Rating Nosedive
item.description: South Korean President Lee Jae Myung will seek to reverse hemorrhaging public support and get his policy agenda back on track at a high-stakes Friday press briefing, even as a barrage of criticism from Donald Trump narrows his room to maneuver.
item.dc:creator: Cat Barton and Soo-Hyang Choi

item.title: Ahead of Midterms, The Battle For America’s Working Class
item.description: Everyone wants the ‘working class’ vote. But in an age of economic uncertainty for many Americans, who does that include?
item.dc:creator: Sarah Holder, Rachael Lewis-Krisky and Brunella Tipismana Urbano

item.title: Trump Hits Trail in North Carolina
item.description: On the early edition of Balance of Power, Bloomberg Washington Correspondents Joe Mathieu and Kailey Leinz discuss President Trump's trip to North Carolina. On today's show, The Cook Political Report Editor Jessica Taylor, Republican Main Street Partnership President and CEO Sarah Chamberlain, Maywood Strategies Principal Doug Farrar and The Rockefeller Foundation President Rajiv Shah. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: US Says Iranian Officials May Travel to New York for UN Meetings
item.description: The Trump administration will allow the core members of an Iranian delegation to travel to the United Nations in New York for the General Assembly next week, the State Department said, even as the US and Iran remain at war in the Middle East.
item.dc:creator: Eric Martin

item.title: Trump Touts ‘Major Progress’ on Plans for New US Base in Poland
item.description: President Donald Trump said “major progress” is being made to establish a new US Army base in Poland, even as the Pentagon plans to reduce American forces in Europe.
item.dc:creator: Ellen Milligan

item.title: Principal's Seema Shah Expects Another Fed Rate Hike This Year (Correct)
item.description: Seema Shah, Principal Asset Management chief global strategist, says markets may be pricing in one more rate hike this year, but October looks likely to be a hold because of the timing of the midterm elections and the possibility of inflation data turns sharply worse. (Corrects name of guest's firm.) (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Merz Says US Friendship Since War ‘Probably Over’ for Now
item.description: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said the era of “unconditional” ties between the US and Europe built since World War II are over, at least for now, the latest pronouncement of a breakdown in relations under Donald Trump’s presidency.
item.dc:creator: Arne Delfs

item.title: Kennedy Center Must Explain Closure as Legal Fight Escalates
item.description: A Washington federal judge ordered the Kennedy Center to provide more information about the recent closure of the decades-old performing arts venue and to notify court challengers about any future “demolition” or broader renovations of the building.
item.dc:creator: Suzanne Monyak

item.title: Lula Boosts Social Welfare Payments Ahead of Tight Election
item.description: Brazil’s government announced an increase to social welfare payments just weeks before a tense election, with polls showing President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva tied with his right-wing challenger.
item.dc:creator: Martha Beck and Beatriz Reis
